No. Do not add Redis.

This system has one writer, restores from SQLite, and needs no cross-host coordination. Redis adds a network dependency, a new failure domain, and an operational burden (persistence config, eviction policy, monitoring) without solving any constraint you have. In a single Elixir process, ETS or GenServer state covers in-memory caching with zero infrastructure cost.

Revisit only if you add a second node or need shared state across hosts.
